before.preferred_name: ATP-binding (nucleotide-binding domain) subunits of MCE-type lipid transport systems: MlaF of the diderm-bacterial Mla pathway, mycobacterial Mkl/MceG, and plant TGD3
before.summary: Stand-alone ABC nucleotide-binding proteins include MlaF, the shared mycobacterial MceG ATPase, plant TGD3 and additional ABC proteins. MlaF supplies ATP-dependent energy to MlaE-containing phospholipid transport assemblies; E. coli MlaB stabilizes the ATPase and supports complex assembly, whereas Bordetella has a characterized F/E/D/A/C locus without an identifiable MlaB. MceG supports fatty-acid and cholesterol uptake systems and TGD3 acts in chloroplast lipid transport. These positive cargo examples do not establish absence of secondary activities. The official SF4 reference branch and current UniProt assignments disagree for some proteins, so neither lipid specificity nor a universal six-component architecture follows from the family label.
before.coherence_reason: The ABC fold and ATP motifs are conserved in the official MSA: all 90 extant reference sequences have a Walker-A candidate, and all four SF4 leaves also have LSGGQ. Cargo and partners differ, and SF4 is not an empty branch. Reference-tree classifications of Q9F3K7 and Q2FVL4 as PTHR43023:SF4 disagree with current UniProt PTHR43166 classifications; both sources are retained without an override.

subfamilies.label: PROTEIN TRIGALACTOSYLDIACYLGLYCEROL 3, CHLOROPLASTIC
subfamilies.description: The subfamily PANTHER names the family after: plant and algal TGD3, the ATPase of the chloroplast inner-envelope TGD1/TGD2/TGD3 lipid importer, together with a set of bacterial paralogs that are not part of the canonical mlaFEDCB operon (Pseudomonas PP_0141 and PA3212, Helicobacter HP_1465, Synechocystis sll1041 and sll1001, Aquifex aq_1531). Bacterial SF3 paralogs do not inherit a chloroplast location from their subfamily name.

node_assessments.assessment_reason: The problem is the term choice, not the node position. GO:1990531 is defined as a protein complex that functions as a phospholipid-translocating P-Type ATPase, i.e. a P4-ATPase flippase complex. Every member of this family is instead the nucleotide-binding subunit of an ABC transporter, so no descendant of this node is part of a P-type ATPase complex and the seed cannot support the term at any node. The seed annotation itself (E. coli MlaF, IPI to the MlaFEDB complex, PMID:27529189) correctly records membership in a transporter complex; what is wrong is the complex type chosen for it, and the IBD carries that error to every bacterial descendant - the Pseudomonas, Haemophilus and Aquifex MlaF proteins and the actinobacterial Mkl/MceG ATPases of the Mce1 and Mce4 importers. GO:0043190 (ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporter complex) is the term that fits, and it holds family-wide. The completed E. coli mlaD and mlaE gene reviews make exactly this replacement. No affected_subfamilies are named because the term is inapplicable throughout rather than in one clade; the taxon-2 scope is incidental here, although it does keep the term off plant TGD3.

before.summary: MCE-domain proteins include the MlaD hexameric phospholipid-binding component and the differentiated MceA-F proteins of mycobacterial lipid import assemblies. E. coli MlaD binds phospholipids, contacts MlaC and caps the MlaE membrane component; the assembled system supports transfer and ATP-dependent retrograde bias. Mycobacterial Mce complexes have distinct fatty-acid/cholesterol uptake roles and extended envelope-spanning architecture. SF4 contains both MlaD and mycobacterial MceD, so an MCE domain or shared subfamily does not identify the Mla substrate or compatible partners. Positive alternate cargo does not establish a secondary phospholipid loss.
before.coherence_reason: The shared property is architectural rather than functional: an MCE domain that oligomerizes into a lipid-conducting ring attached to an ABC transporter. Beyond that, the family lumps at least three functionally distinct groups. (i) MlaD and its diderm-bacterial orthologs bind phospholipids and work in outer-membrane lipid asymmetry maintenance. (ii) The mycobacterial Mce proteins of SF15-SF19, and the mycobacterial members of SF4, are substrate-binding subunits of importers for host fatty acids and cholesterol, located in the cell wall rather than at the plasma membrane, with roles in host interaction and persistence; phospholipid-specific terms do not hold for them. (iii) Within that mycobacterial set, only the Mce1 clade has any evidence bearing on host-cell entry, and the actinobacterial relatives in Streptomyces coelicolor - a soil saprophyte with no host - inherit host-interaction terms they cannot possibly perform. Subfamily boundaries follow operon position, not function, so SF4 contains both E. coli MlaD and mycobacterial Mce1D/Mce2D/Mce3D/Mce4D.

Resolving this needs a curator with the Mce1A primary literature in hand; until then no subfamily scope is asserted, and a gene review for any member should treat the term as unsettled rather than inherited.
